## Brief
SCOPE NARROWED 2026-09-16 (Eric): the WEB client only. renderer/app.js is out of your deliverables — do not touch it. Its identical fix is recorded on BAD-041, the ticket that splits renderer/app.js, and lands with that split. If you have already edited renderer/app.js, revert it (`git checkout -- renderer/app.js`) and carry on.

Say in refreshCollab what BAD-090 said in runCollabSync: supersession cancels the PAINT, not the TRANSFER.

refreshCollab(pack, {pull:true}) is how a scene ARRIVES in a room, and its pull sits BELOW the `seq !== collab.seq` guard. onSceneSelected/selectPack fires it un-awaited, so any caller that bumps collab.seq in the window between the info read and the pull abandons the arrival pull with no retry and no error — and the superseding refresh passes pull:false, so it fetches nothing. The person who just opened a collab scene sees an empty room for up to the 60s poll. autoPullWrapped is worse: collabAutoPulled makes it once per room per run, so its single pull being superseded means the wrapped room's takes never get a second attempt at all.

In web/collabweb-model.js the guard is the `if (seq !== collab.seq || ...) return false;` after the `info` fetch; the pull branch is `if (pull && !collab.offline) { ... }` below it.

The shape BAD-090 settled on is the reference: runCollabSync in web/collabweb-sync.js guards the transfer on scene identity only ((state.scene && state.scene.id) === sceneId), never on collab.seq, and leaves the seq check for the repaint. Read test/collabreads.test.js's head comment before you write anything — it is the written record of why the read sits where it sits, and its 'a focus poll landing mid-cycle does not cancel the cycle`s pull' test is the identical mechanism for the sync path.

Decide, and write the reason down where the next person will hit it:
- Which conditions still cancel the pull. Scene identity must; collab.seq must not. `collab.offline` and `collabActive()` are read before the pull today — say what they mean once the pull moves above the guard.
- What the superseded call returns and what it must NOT leave behind. A superseded refresh still returns false, and must not toast, must not overwrite collab.remote/collab.resolved, must not repaint or re-arm the poll on top of a newer call's state. The pull's WRITES go to the take store and are wanted whoever asked for them; the paint is the part that belongs to the current call only.
- Whether moving the pull above the guard changes the wire order BAD-090 pinned. It must not: the read stays at the tail of the sync cycle and before the first download-url. If your change moves a read, you have changed BAD-090's invariant and the answer is a different fix, not a relaxed test.

The desktop client keeps the old shape on purpose, so say so in a comment at the web fix: the two clients now differ here, renderer/app.js carries the same bug, and BAD-041 holds the fix. A reader who finds the divergence must not "helpfully" restore it.

Extend test/collabreads.test.js (do not start a new file): a web test proving an arrival pull survives a concurrent seq bump — the takes land in the remote store — and one proving the superseded call still does not paint. Build the broken version first and confirm your new tests fail on it; a test that passes both ways is worth nothing here, which is exactly the trap BAD-090's reviewer caught. The file's existing structural assertions over renderer/app.js pin BAD-090's shape there and must keep passing untouched.

Spawn ONE reviewer as your child (persona reviewer, model opus) before you return, and give it the diff, this brief and BAD-090's outcome. BAD-090's first cut was blocked by its reviewer for this precise class of mistake — a supersession guard wrapping a transfer — so the review is the part of this ticket most likely to earn its cost. Wait for it inside your turn and act on what it says.

## Result
Web arrival pull fixed and pinned. web/collabweb-model.js: refreshCollab is now three parts with three guards — ABSORB (collab.info/skew/hbPhase, taken by whichever read landed last, kept monotonic by a new collab.readSeq, and deliberately ABOVE the seq check because pullTakes decides from collab.info and a pull without one would open the bootstrap read BAD-090 deleted); PAINT (loading, renders, collab.remote/resolved, toast, poll — the current call's alone, and a superseded refresh still returns false); TRANSFER (the pull, cancelled by IDENTITY only). Identity is scene AND room: here() captures roomId = collab.pin.id, because a scene carries two pins and a newer refresh can dropPin one without changing the scene — that was the reviewer's blocker, where a late read otherwise left collab.pin and collab.info naming two different rooms with collabActive() true across the pair. A superseded call whose pull actually landed takes does run the transfer's tail (list, resolve, repaint) and only it: without that the takes reach disk and the room still looks empty, which is the symptom the ticket exists to fix, and it is the same three lines runCollabSync runs after its own pull. The pull gate is now 'pull && res.ok' rather than '!collab.offline' so a NEWER call's failed read cannot cancel this call's transfer (identical for the current call). Two decisions worth Spud's eye: the transfer's tail, and writing the snapshot from a superseded call at all. test/collabreads.test.js: three new executed tests plus a rewritten structural pin; the harness gained a held read, a per-read mark and two counters. RED PROVEN — on HEAD's model the two executed tests and the structural one fail (wire is 'info -> info', no download-url at all) while all ten pre-existing tests still pass; the room-identity test is killed by mutating the room term back out. Verified: node --test test/collabreads.test.js 14/14 (three consecutive runs, no flake); npm test 1850 tests / 1728 pass / 0 fail / 122 skipped, exit 0, voicepacks linked so the pack tests were not vacuous; and per web/CLAUDE.md (no smoke leg for web/) the page was booted from THIS worktree on a private port 8931 rather than the shared 8901 entry — every collabweb-* script 200, refreshCollab/runCollabSync/wireCollab defined, collab.readSeq present, only three pre-existing 404s for generated files. renderer/app.js untouched per the narrowed scope; the file's existing structural pins over it still pass and now also record the divergence and BAD-041. collabweb-model.js is 376 lines (was 259, ~85 of the 117 added lines are the comment explaining the rule) and stays one job: the web collab client's state and status. ## Outcome
Accepted. The change says more than the ticket asked for and is better for it: the ticket proposed moving the pull above the seq check, and Vitelotte found that doing so needs a second sequence (collab.readSeq) to keep the snapshot monotonic, or a late read replaces a newer one's answer. Its reviewer Mozart then blocked the first cut on a real defect the ticket did not foresee — identity here is the scene AND the room, because a scene carries two pins, so a read against a room a newer refresh had dropPinned was being absorbed anyway, leaving collab.pin and collab.info naming different rooms with collabActive() true across the pair. All four findings actioned. Two judgment calls I agree with: a superseded call whose pull landed still runs the transfer's tail, because without it the takes reach disk and the room still looks empty, which is the bug over again; and the pull gate moved from !collab.offline to res.ok, since collab.offline on a superseded call is a newer call's verdict and a verdict is not an identity change. Red was proven per test on HEAD's model, and the divergence from renderer/app.js is commented at the fix and pinned on both sides.
